articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally turned GitHub into a government secrets buffet, exposing AWS GovCloud keys and internal systems. When the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own contractors, you know we're living in the best timeline.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor publicly hosted AWS GovCloud credentials on GitHub like it's a recipe blog. The agency responsible for national cybersecurity just served up privileged access keys with a side of institutional incompetence.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates another win for end-to-end encryption, the digital equivalent of whispering secrets that actually stay secret. In a world where privacy is treated like a luxury good, every encrypted message is an act of rebellion.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF drops a new guide on fighting surveillance abuses because apparently we need instruction manuals for basic human rights now. When digital surveillance becomes normalized, resistance becomes a civic duty.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google's 'instant' API key deletion is about as instant as a Windows update—researchers found keys stay active for 23 minutes after 'deletion.' Cloud providers lying about security features is basically a Tuesday at this point.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Trump Mobile website was hemorrhaging customer data to anyone who could craft an HTTP request. The same crowd that screams about election security can't secure a basic web form—poetry in motion.

articles.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI discovered 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities in widely-used software within a month. When AI becomes better at finding bugs than human security teams, it's either revolution or unemployment—possibly both.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms two major Defender security issues — so update now or face possible attack
articles.summary: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin vulnerability scores a perfect 10.0 CVSS and gets exploited in the wild for root access. Maximum severity, maximum chaos, maximum 'told you so' energy from every security researcher who saw this coming.

articles.title: GitHub Confirms 3,800 Internal Repos Stolen Through Poisoned VS Code Extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP hacker group is poisoning open source code at industrial scale, turning trusted repositories into malware distribution networks. Supply chain attacks are the new normal, and trust is officially a deprecated concept.

articles.title: Update Chrome now: Critical bugs could let attackers run code
articles.summary: GitHub confirms 3,800 internal repos stolen via poisoned VS Code extension, proving even the house of code isn't safe from social engineering. TeamPCP just turned Microsoft's own development tools against them—chef's kiss level of irony.
